question: When a fair six-sided die is tossed on a table top, the bottom face cannot be seen. What is the probability that the product of the numbers on the five faces that can be seen is divisible by \(6?\)
solution:
Only one of the numbers \(1,2,3,4,5,6\) is hidden. Separate the possibilities according to whether \(6\) is visible.

If \(6\) is visible, the product contains a factor of \(6\), so it is divisible by \(6\). If \(6\) is hidden, both \(2\) and \(3\) are visible, and their product supplies the factor \(2\cdot3=6\).

These cases cover every toss, so the product is always divisible by \(6\). The probability is \(1\), choice \(E\).
